experiment_template.research_question: Does demand-driven recovery improve complete-task quality and cumulative token efficiency over repaired eager recovery at8K?
stop_conditions: 128MiB evidence; monitored2GiB source envelope;1GiB D and8GiB guest reserve; C excluded
Four fixed tasks/eight arms; no retries, replacements or failed-task deletion
Maximum512index tokenizer calls and291request tokenizer calls per arm; one transport attempt
Native references accessed only by isolated scoring after sealed generation
Shared stop on source/storage/provider/accounting failure; settle workers and retain all costs
Two workers; maximum96model calls and96000model tokens per arm;768calls/768000tokens overall

records.falsifier: A complete valid known-cost comparison misses either perfect treatment quality or15% total savings. Infrastructure,unknown usage or missing outcomes are inconclusive.
records.mechanism: Keep source tools,discovery retention,compact cursor,freshness,output policy,budgets and terminal base-valid-handles-v2 selection fixed. Vary only eager catalog/schema visibility versus demand entry/opening. Measure actual opening and repeated-exploration costs.
records.scope: Four exposed development tasks; complete fresh paired trajectories. Broader untouched confirmation still required.
records.statement: Demand-driven recovery achieves perfect treatment Span-F1/File-F1 on every fixed task while reducing cumulative model tokens by at least15% against repaired eager recovery.
